examples.label: Find .kdbx files on a Windows target (PowerShell)
Extract the KeePass hash (modern keepass2john as system tool)
Find hashcat mode number on exam day

notes:
=== KeePass Database Cracking — keepass2john + Hashcat ===
Convert KeePass .kdbx to crackable hash, then crack offline for access to entire credential vault.

=== TECHNICAL BACKGROUND ===
KeePass .kdbx files: locally stored password vaults protected by master password (and optionally key file)
Encryption: AES-256 with PBKDF2 or Argon2 key derivation (slow to crack by design)
keepass2john: extracts the key derivation parameters and encrypted data into hashcat format
Hashcat mode 13400: targets KeePass encryption scheme

=== WORKFLOW ===
Step 1: Find .kdbx files
  Get-ChildItem -Path C:\ -Recurse -Include *.kdbx -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Also check: Dropbox, OneDrive, SharePoint sync directories

Step 2: Transfer .kdbx to attack host

Step 3: Convert to crackable hash
  python3 keepass2john.py Database.kdbx > keepass.hash
  cat keepass.hash   → verify hash extracted successfully

Step 4: Crack with Hashcat
  hashcat -m 13400 keepass.hash /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
  hashcat -m 13400 keepass.hash /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule

Step 5: Open with cracked password
  Use KeePass client on any machine → all stored credentials accessible

=== VALUE OF A CRACKED KEEPASS DB ===
IT staff KeePass = entire organization's infrastructure credentials in one file
Commonly contains: network devices, servers, domain controllers, cloud accounts, vendor access
Single cracked database can yield: router passwords, firewall credentials, all server admin passwords

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
.kdbx found on file share → transfer + crack → mass credential exposure → full environment access
KeePass with key file requirement → key file often in same directory or user profile
KeePass master password = often same as user's Windows password → try their NTLM hash offline
After DA: search all file shares for .kdbx files → may find multiple databases from different admins

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
.kdbx files on shared drives (IT teams share KeePass databases across the team)
KeePass.exe in installed software (wmic product) → user definitely has a database
Keepass2.xml config file → reveals database file path
Key files (.keyx) in same directories → required for decryption alongside password Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 15 (Password Attacks).
name: Credential Hunting - Crack KeePass Database
description: Extract a crackable hash from a found .kdbx KeePass database and brute-force the master password offline with hashcat mode 13400.

defense.why_it_works: KeePass .kdbx database files are protected by a master password. keepass2john extracts the key derivation parameters and password hash into a crackable format. Hashcat with mode 13400 then applies wordlist or rule-based attacks against this hash. If the master password is weak or found in common wordlists (rockyou), the entire secrets database is recovered.
defense.prerequisites: Read access to a .kdbx file (find on share or local filesystem). keepass2john.py tool. hashcat with appropriate wordlist. Sufficient compute for cracking.
defense.impact: Full recovery of all secrets stored in KeePass database: passwords, SSH keys, API tokens, RDP credentials — enabling complete credential compromise for all accounts the owner managed.
defense.detection: KeePass database file read by non-owner user. keepass2john.py execution. Hashcat workload on suspect system. Transfer of .kdbx file to attacker-controlled system.
defense.artifacts: File access log: .kdbx read by non-owner | Process: keepass2john.py executed | Network: .kdbx file transferred to attacker IP
defense.prevention: Use strong master passwords (20+ characters, random). Enable KeePass key file in addition to master password (two-factor). Restrict file permissions on .kdbx databases. Do not leave KeePass databases on shared drives. Enable KeePass security auditing features.
defense.misconfiguration: KeePass database file stored on a network share or in a world-readable location. Weak master password chosen for convenience. No key file used as second factor.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# KeePass DB accessible to attacker:
Get-ChildItem C:\Users\ -Recurse -Filter *.kdbx
# Found: C:\Users\htb-student\Documents\ILFREIGHT_Help_Desk.kdbx

# Extract and crack:
python2.7 keepass2john.py ILFREIGHT_Help_Desk.kdbx > hash.txt
hashcat -m 13400 hash.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict KeePass database permissions
icacls ILFREIGHT_Help_Desk.kdbx /inheritance:r /grant 'htb-student:(R)'

# Enforce strong master password + key file
# KeePass: Security > Password Quality (enforce minimum entropy)

# Store KeePass DB only in encrypted locations (BitLocker drive)
# Never on world-accessible network shares
